title: Financial Assistance Program Terms: The Financial Hardship Plan of the Patient Payment Plans
content:
The Financial Hardship Plan is the tier of the Patient Payment Plans reserved for patients with a current hardship approval, and it is available only with that approval, as required when a plan is proposed. It differs from the other tiers in three ways.

**Term 1. Pauses.** Where the tier permits pauses, the patient may pause installments for up to the tier's longest pause, in consecutive months, at most the tier's maximum number of pauses, while the plan is active and current. The paused months are added to the end of the term, and nothing is missed during them.

**Term 2. Review.** The plan is reviewed the tier's review period, in calendar months, after signing. If the hardship approval has expired by then, the remaining balance is re-spread under the plan's own terms without a pause option; the plan is never moved to another tier.

**Term 3. Add-ons.** Its add-ons restart the term.

**Term 4. Patients on other tiers.** A patient on any other tier who experiences hardship is not moved to the Financial Hardship Plan by a modification; a new plan after cancellation is required.

### Review outcome

| Hardship approval at the review | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Expired | Remaining balance re-spread under the plan's own terms, without a pause option; the plan stays on the Financial Hardship Plan |

### Pause conditions

| Condition for a pause | Required |
|---|---|
| Plan status | Active |
| Installments | Current |
| Length | No more than the tier's longest pause, in consecutive months |
| Number | Within the tier's maximum pauses over the plan's life |

### Illustration (hypothetical)

A patient on the 24-Month Extended Plan reports a job loss and asks to be moved to the Financial Hardship Plan. A modification cannot make that move; the Financial Hardship Plan would require a new plan after the 24-Month Extended Plan is cancelled.
